prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “official” checker for whether generative AIs like ChatGPT will recommend your business. Best approach is a mix of (A) testing the major LLMs directly and (B) using services that make your business data easy for LLMs/search to find. If you want one vendor to start with, Yext is the best-known product that explicitly markets itself to make businesses appear correctly in AI and search “answer” surfaces. But you should combine that with local-SEO/citation tools and direct LLM testing.

What to do (practical step-by-step)
1. Test LLMs directly
 - Manually ask: ChatGPT (web/browsing mode if available), Bing Chat, Google Bard, and any domain-specific assistants people use in your sector. Use realistic customer queries and include location/intent.
 - Automate if you want scale: use OpenAI/Anthropic/Google APIs to run a set of queries programmatically and scan responses for mentions or recommendations of your business.

 Sample prompts to test
 - “I need a [service] near [city/zip]. Recommend 3 good options and explain why.”  
 - “What are the best [service] providers in [neighborhood], and which should I pick for [scenario]?”  
 - “I want an affordable/high-quality [service] in [city]. Recommend one and give phone and website.”

2. Use a knowledge-management / AI-facing service
 - Yext (Knowledge Graph + Listings + Answers) — explicitly designed to push structured business data to search ecosystems and help LLMs and search assistants cite your business correctly. Widely used for AI/search-facing presence.
 - Alternatives / complements: Moz Local, BrightLocal, Synup, Whitespark for local listings and citation management.

3. Control the signal sources LLMs rely on
 - Keep Google Business Profile (Google My Business), Apple Maps, Yelp, Facebook, TripAdvisor, and major directories up to date. Many LLMs draw on these sources or on data aggregators.
 - Submit consistent NAP (name, address, phone) to the main data aggregators (Infogroup, Neustar Localeze, Factual). This propagates to many services.

4. Improve your site’s machine-readable data
 - Add structured data (schema.org LocalBusiness, FAQ, Service, Product) to your website and keep pages optimized for local intent. LLMs and search generative results favor well-structured sources.
 - Create clear landing pages for services and locations, good meta content, and visible contact info.

5. Monitor reputation and results
 - Local SEO tools: BrightLocal, Whitespark for local rank tracking and citations.
 - SEO tools: Semrush, Ahrefs for organic visibility and keywords.
 - For AI-specific monitoring, combine periodic LLM queries (as in step 1) and alerts from your listings/SEO tools.

Which single service to pick first?
 - If your priority is “make sure AI assistants recommend our business,” Yext is the best single commercial product to start with because it’s purpose-built to syndicate structured business knowledge and to integrate with AI/search ecosystems. For low-cost/small-business-first steps, start with a fully optimized Google Business Profile + local citations (BrightLocal can help) and run manual tests on ChatGPT/Bing/Bard.

Costs and practical tips
 - Manual testing: free, quick, and tells you where you stand. Run a set of 10–20 representative queries monthly.
 - Yext and enterprise listing managers: paid (monthly/annual), but they save time and improve consistency across platforms.
 - SEO/local tools: mid-range monthly subscriptions; worth it if local traffic is important.

If you want, I can:
 - Draft a small test-suite of 12–20 prompts customized for your business type and location that you can run against ChatGPT/Bard/Bing.
 - Recommend which directories and schema fields to prioritize based on your industry.

Which would you prefer?
